external_entities.name: Remote Peer Node
external_entities.description: Remote Ethereum node in P2P network communication
external_entities.rationale: Network peers can be malicious, send invalid data, or attempt protocol attacks. All P2P communications must be validated.

boundary_interactions.interaction: Peer sends response with echoed request_id

external_entities.name: Transaction Sender
external_entities.description: External account initiating contract creation transaction
external_entities.rationale: Any external account can submit transactions. Malicious actors may attempt to exploit contract creation at addresses with residual storage.

external_entities.name: Malicious Actor
external_entities.description: Attacker attempting to exploit protocol vulnerabilities
external_entities.rationale: Explicitly modeled adversary in security boundary subgraphs. Represents worst-case threat actor.

boundary_interactions.interaction: Submit deployment transaction targeting residual address

external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter
external_entities.description: User or application submitting type-4 transaction via JSON-RPC
external_entities.rationale: Transaction submitters are unauthenticated external parties. Must validate all transaction data.

boundary_interactions.interaction: User submits type-4 transaction via RPC

external_entities.name: External Caller
external_entities.description: Contract or EOA making a call to a delegated account
external_entities.rationale: Any contract or EOA can call delegated accounts. Callers may be malicious contracts attempting to exploit delegation.

boundary_interactions.interaction: Implicit: initiates CALL to delegated EOA

external_entities.name: EIP Author
external_entities.description: External party proposing an Ethereum Improvement Proposal
external_entities.rationale: EIP authors are external parties. Proposals must be reviewed by the community before acceptance.

external_entities.name: Core Developers
external_entities.description: Ethereum client developers responsible for implementing consensus changes
external_entities.rationale: Core developers have established track record but their proposals still require community review. Disagreements can cause network partitioning.

misclassified_entities.original_description: Local client component initiating eth protocol requests
misclassified_entities.reason: This is an internal client component, not an external entity. It represents the local node's request initiation logic.

misclassified_entities.original_description: Contract executing CREATE or CREATE2 opcode
misclassified_entities.reason: This represents internal EVM execution of opcodes, not an external entity. The contract is already within the EVM execution context.

trust_boundary_edges.validation_required: Request ID correlation, RLP structure validation, payload validation
RLP decoding, request ID format validation
Transaction format validation, authorization list validation, signature verification
Nonce matching, signature verification, chain ID validation
Consensus review, implementation agreement across clients

gaps.gap: No explicit edge from external entity to subgraph - implicitly enters through contract creation initiation

security_observations.observation: EIP-7702 introduces significant new attack surface through authorization replay and tx.origin invariant breaking
security_observations.mitigation: Nonce-based replay protection, explicit security boundary modeling

security_observations.observation: EIP-7610 addresses residual storage attack vector with only 28 known vulnerable addresses on mainnet
security_observations.mitigation: Storage emptiness validation before contract creation

security_observations.observation: P2P protocol communications (eth/64, eth/66) assume peers may be malicious
security_observations.mitigation: ForkID validation, request ID correlation, message structure validation

security_observations.observation: EIP-4 governance process acknowledges risk of network partitioning from consensus disagreements
